continuation_of: Batch 27 review recorded 2026-11-03; this is a follow-up evidence refresh, not a new country count.

findings.source: INSTAT Mali National Data Archive, EAC 2023-2024 related materials
observations: Official CPS/SDR report is available as a 3.56 MB PDF (catalogue download identifier 969); the catalogue contents page lists crop area, crop yields, input use, cereal area/output, legumes, oilseeds, livestock, poultry and fisheries chapters.
The EAC includes cultivated area by crop, yields, fertilizer/pesticide use, farm equipment, livestock and commercialization. A separate yield-plot questionnaire (Q5RDT) is listed.
The report itself could not be downloaded through the current retrieval route during this review; therefore no new crop-specific table values are transcribed or accepted.

findings.topic: EAC 2023-2024 public microdata metadata and survey design
observations: The public release is anonymised version 2.1 and includes over 8,000 agricultural holdings, selected through a two-stage stratified design with 740 enumeration areas and regions as strata.
Coverage excludes Kidal for security reasons; Bamako District is also excluded because agricultural activity is limited.
The catalogue reports first-stage EA coverage of 86%, holding coverage of 79.4%, and second-round coverage of 58.3%; weights are distinct for Passage 1 and Passage 2.

Modules include plots and crop areas, fertilizer/pesticide inputs, labour, commercialization, livestock, poultry, equipment, and measured yield plots. GPS plot measurement and weighed crop-cut harvests were used.

The catalogue states that microdata are anonymised but subject to CPS/SDR confidentiality and use conditions: publish only aggregated results, do not redistribute respondent-level records, and submit derived reports to CPS/SDR.

findings.source: Mali Ministry of Economy and Finance / DGMP, Mercuriale des prix: Bamako and regional capitals 2026
observations: The ministry catalogue lists a 2026 bulletin for Bamako and separate regional bulletins for Badiangara, Bougouni, Dioila, Douentza, Gao, Kayes, Kidal, Kita, Koulikoro, Koutiala, Menaka, Mopti, Nara, Nioro, San, Ségou, Sikasso, Taoudenit and Tombouctou.
A directly retrievable 2026 Tombouctou PDF confirms that the tables are public procurement/retail reference prices with minimum, mean and maximum TTC prices, not farm-gate producer prices.

This collection is useful as a regional cost-reference lead for selected purchased goods/services only after relevant agricultural items are identified; it must not be used as a farmer's actual input bill without product, quality, tax and delivery matching.

findings.source: World Bank Microdata Library, Mali Monthly food price estimates by product and market
observations: Latest catalogue version reviewed is 2026-10-05, with monthly estimates through 2026-10-01, 136 Mali markets, 32,606 pooled cases and 95 variables.
Fields include administrative region, market name, price date, currency, data coverage, confidence score, spatial interpolation flag and commodity series for beans, maize, millet, rice and sorghum.
The dataset is market-level estimated food prices, not direct farm-gate quotations; retain confidence/coverage/interpolation flags and separate retail/market prices from producer prices.
In Mali, wholesale millet and sorghum prices in September 2026 were generally up to 25% below year-earlier levels, supported by carryover stocks after the above-average 2025 harvest.
Conflict-affected Gao and Tombouctou continued to record substantially higher prices than other monitored markets because of disrupted trade and depleted household stocks.

findings.topic: 2025 campaign output and 2026 support-price policy cross-check
findings.source: Government of Mali CENA report, 3 April 2026; ORTM CSA report, 9 June 2026
observations: Government reported 2025 aggregate cereal output of 11,452,540 tonnes; this is a national aggregate, not a crop-specific yield.
For the 2026/27 campaign, ORTM reports first-grade seed cotton at FCFA 300/kg, mineral fertilizer at FCFA 15,000 per 50 kg bag and organic fertilizer at FCFA 3,000 per 50 kg bag.
These are campaign policy/support prices. Fertilizer formulation, eligibility, distribution, timing and last-mile farmer cost must be checked before budgeting.

remaining_gaps: Download and extract the CPS/SDR EAC 2023-2024 report tables and authorized anonymised microdata aggregates; apply the correct passage-specific survey weights and report confidence/precision.
Keep Kidal excluded from EAC-based regional estimates unless an independent, valid Kidal source is obtained; distinguish Bamako District from the 19 regions.

Extract relevant agricultural products and services from the 2026 DGMP regional procurement bulletins, but classify them only as public procurement reference prices unless matched farmer transaction evidence exists.
Extract the World Bank RTFP market/commodity CSV by market and month, preserve coverage/confidence/interpolation fields, and label all results as estimated market prices rather than farm-gate prices.
Obtain dated crop-specific producer prices by region, grade and product form; the March 2025 rice farm-gate price in the earlier USDA report is historical only.
Build regional budgets for seed, fertilizer, crop protection, labour, machinery, irrigation, energy, transport and livestock feed, using observed farmer-paid costs.
Validate the current 17 commodity mappings, production systems, XOF currency handling and regional test cases before activation.
calculator_decision: No activation. Mali remains research-only. The new evidence strengthens the survey and regional price-source plan, but no crop-specific values were extracted from the EAC tables, no current crop-specific farm-gate price set was validated, and no complete regional enterprise budgets exist.
